ashby:1password:3b1dd358-261b-440e-9277-.summary: 1Password is growing. We’ve surpassed $500M in ARR and we’re continuing to accelerate, earning a spot on the Forbes Cloud 100 for four years in a row and teaming up with iconic partners like Oracle Red Bull Racing.

sections.title: About 1Password
paras: At 1Password, we’re building the foundation for a safe, productive digital future. Our mission is to unleash employee productivity without compromising security by ensuring every identity is authentic, every application sign-in is secure, and every device is trusted. We innovated the market-leading enterprise password manager and pioneered Unified Access Management, a new cybersecurity category built for the way people and AI agents work today. As one of the most loved brands in cybersecurity, we take a human-centric approach in everything from product strategy to user experience. Over 180,000 businesses, from Fortune 100 leaders to the world’s most innovative AI companies, trust 1Password to help their teams securely adopt the SaaS and AI tools they need to do their best work.

If you're excited about the opportunity to contribute to the digital safety of millions, to work alongside a team of curious, driven individuals, and to solve hard problems in a fast-paced, dynamic environment, then we want to hear from you. Come join us and help shape a safer, simpler digital future.

As a Senior Implementation Consultant on the Customer Success team, you’ll lead technical deployments and customer enablement for 1Password’s product suite, partnering with Project Managers, Technical Account Managers, and Solutions Architects to deliver successful outcomes for commercial and enterprise customers. You’ll combine hands-on configuration, project management, customer training, and technical guidance to help organizations adopt secure, effective ways of working. Your work will help customers protect access to the tools and information they rely on every day, advancing 1Password’s mission to make life easier and safer for everyone.

sections.title: How we’re using AI today
paras: Across GTM, we’re transforming the way we work with AI. We expect every seller, CSM, and team member to become a power user, using it daily to work smarter and move faster. AI is already embedded in how we operate – from real-time coaching that sharpens how we sell and interact with customers, to surfacing insights that help us anticipate needs – creating more time for meaningful customer engagement. If you’re excited to reshape how you think, make decisions, and drive growth with AI, you’ll feel right at home here.
This is a remote opportunity within Canada and the US.

sections.title: What we're looking for:
bullets: Combine strong technical aptitude with project management experience, including managing timelines, coordinating stakeholders, tracking time, and monitoring utilization.
Configure solutions and answer complex customer questions independently, knowing when to involve the right internal partners.

Understand identity and security concepts such as identity providers (IdPs), Single Sign-On (SSO), System for Cross-domain Identity Management (SCIM), Active Directory, Mobile Device Management (MDM), and Zero Trust.
Communicate clearly with technical practitioners, senior stakeholders, and audiences with different levels of technical knowledge.
Design and deliver engaging virtual and in-person training for enterprise administrators, executives, and end users.
Use artificial intelligence (AI), automation, and workflow improvements thoughtfully to reduce repetitive work and create reusable solutions.

sections.title: What you can expect:
paras: USA-based roles only: The annual base salary for this role is between $102,000 USD and $148,000 USD, and is commission-eligible. This role is also eligible for immediate participation in 1Password's benefits program (health, dental, 401k and many others), utilization of our generous paid time off, an equity grant and, where applicable, participation in our incentive programs.

Canada-based roles only: The annual base salary for this role is between $102,000 CAD and $148,000 CAD and is commission-eligible. This role is also eligible for immediate participation in 1Password’s generous benefits program (health, dental, RRSP and many others), utilization of our generous paid time off, an equity grant and, where applicable, participation in our incentive programs.

At 1Password, we approach each individual's compensation with a promise of fair market value and internal equity commensurate with experience and specific skill set.

This posting is for an existing vacancy.

Our culture
At 1Password, we prioritize collaboration, clear and transparent communication, receptiveness to feedback, and alignment with our core values: keep it simple, lead with honesty, and put people first.

You’ll be part of a team that challenges the status quo, and is excited to experiment and iterate in search of the best solution. That said, 1Password is not for everyone . Our work is demanding, we strive for excellence, and the pace is fast. We need people who are keen to take on challenging problems, who seek feedback to grow, and who are driven to make an impact. If you're looking for a place where you can settle into a comfortable routine, this might not be the right fit for you. We’re looking for individuals who are proven experts in their fields, as well as those who are highly adaptable, can thrive in ambiguity and through change, are curious, and above all deliver results.

How we work with AI
We are committed to leveraging cutting-edge technology—including AI—to achieve our mission. We also understand that thinking critically about AI in its current forms will help us create better solutions for our customers and ourselves with its future forms, which will help us continue to close the gap between security and privacy and achieve our mission. We want team members at all levels to take the approach of actively learning AI best practices, identifying opportunities to apply AI in meaningful ways, and driving innovative solutions in their daily work. Embracing the future of AI isn't just encouraged—it's an essential part of how we will be successful at 1Password.
bullets: Lead the hands-on configuration, integration, validation, and launch of 1Password’s Enterprise Password Manager, SaaS Manager, Device Trust, and Unified Access.

ashby:alpacahealth:fc1f5e8e-c448-4018-b6.summary:
Alpaca Health enables clinicians to become entrepreneurs, starting in autism care.

We help clinicians launch and scale their own clinics by providing AI-powered software, payer contracting, and full back-office infrastructure. Our goal is simple: shift power in healthcare away from large consolidated entities and back to clinicians.

Our product is a complex marketplace business. For providers, we manage the insurance operations and back office admin of their business. For patients, we act as a front door to finding a best-fit therapist. And, we accomplish this by having an operations team, enabled by best-in-class software.

sections.title: 📌 About Alpaca Health
paras: We are growing quickly and expanding into new states this year. The problems we are solving are operationally complex, high-stakes, and deeply meaningful for families.

We've raised over $14M in funding from early-stage investors like Core Innovation Capital, Adverb Ventures, and South Park Commons, and are building for long-term category leadership. More importantly, we're serving hundreds of patients, while growing 30% MoM.

sections.title: 🎯 Role: Founding Product Manager
paras: We are hiring a Head of Product to build an AI-native platform that powers every side of our market: providers, families, and our internal operations team.

We're not looking for a traditional Head of Product. There's been no PM at Alpaca to date: Operations Leads have worked directly with Engineers to build product. We believe that's what an AI-native product organization looks like: less and less separation between the business and building.

But our product is getting more complex — more stakeholders, more capabilities, more integrations — while engineering velocity keeps increasing. That demands real thought around launch plans, knowledge base quality, QA, and more. And it means building the shared product sense across Operations Leads — so good judgment doesn't depend on you being in every room

sections.title: What You’ll Do
paras: You have taste, and that shows in our products for patients (B2C), providers (B2B) and internal operations teams (internal tools).

You care about the details of user flows and design, not just whether a feature works. Healthcare has trained patients and providers to expect clunky portals and forms that ask the same question five times. We think that's a failure of imagination, not a fact of the industry. Families and clinicians deserve the same craft as any consumer app they use, and you're offended on their behalf when healthcare software falls short. You can hire and manage design talent that meets your own bar.

sections.title: Build for the whole business, not just the app.
paras: We are fundamentally an operations business. We sell the outcome to our provider entrepreneurs (done for you healthcare admin), and accomplish the outcome more efficiently than competitors with AI enablement. This means that internal tools are a core part of our product. You should love designing integrations with HubSpot, or our own internal CRMs, where our ops teams across client intake, prior authorizations, revenue cycle, provider success, and more actually live.

ashby:duet:e67baf34-cd56-444a-b813-8d670.summary:
Duet is proving that nurse-practitioner-led care isn't just more accessible, it's better. We help NPs build and scale independent practices in communities too often overlooked by the health system: rural towns, immigrant populations, LGBTQ+ patients, and more. Backed by AI-driven tools that give independent NPs the backing of a much bigger system, our network of 100+ practices covering 400,000 annual visits has driven a 30% increase in preventative visits and a 35% drop in hospitalizations, the clearest sign yet that localized NP-led care means better outcomes.

We're a well-funded, early-stage company led by seasoned entrepreneurs and nurse practitioners, and backed by investors including Lerer Hippeau and Kairos.

sections.title: Why Duet, Why Now
paras: Independent primary care is disappearing, swallowed by hospital systems and private equity roll-ups, often pulling out of the communities that need it most. But 31 states now support autonomous NP practice, and the results back up what we've long believed. We built the first value-based care contracts for NPs with major payors, taking on real financial risk for outcomes. In our anchor market in New Hampshire, our network outperformed the state on total cost of care by 19%, proof that a solo NP in an underserved area can outperform a system ten times their size and get rewarded for it.

sections.title: About the Role
paras: Today NPs come to Duet to launch their clinics for its community of owners, special vendor deals, enhanced payor contracts, and advisor guidance.

Your job is to productize this experience. You'll sit close enough to the work to understand it in detail: sitting in on practice onboarding, watching how practice advisors actually spend a Tuesday, working with credentialing and billing. From there you’ll lead building the systems, workflows, and products that make the next launch faster and more delightful.

This is a 0-to-1 role in the real sense: how does a new practice acquire its first hundred patients, and which of those channels can be managed at scale? What does a launching practice actually need to see and do each week, and how much of that can our product guide them vs an advisor? You'll form opinions on these, design experiments to test them, and work with engineers to build what survives contact with reality.

sections.title: What You'll Do
bullets: Live inside the launch process. Shadow the practice advisors, join practice calls, sit with credentialing, billing, and EHR onboarding. Build a first-hand map of where a launch can stall, what gets repeated, and which pain is loudest for the NP versus most expensive for us.

Own the launch product roadmap. Turn what you learn into a prioritized set of bets across internal tooling, practice-facing product, and automation. Write the specs, make the tradeoffs, and defend the sequencing.

Build the practice-facing experience. Shape what a launching practice sees, does, and gets nudged toward in our product during their first ninety days, so the product carries more of the relationship over time.
Test community and cohort models. Explore whether launching NPs get more from each other than from us — cohort programming, peer content, shared playbooks — and build the ones that show signal.

Work directly with engineers. Partner with a small team to scope, ship, and iterate. Prototype yourself where it's faster. Be technical enough to be useful in a design discussion and honest about tradeoffs.

Hand off cleanly. Get each piece of the Launcher experience to the point where it's documented, instrumented, and stable enough to transition to our core product team, then go find the next bottleneck.

sections.title: KPIs You'll Own
bullets: Time to launch: days from signed agreement to first patient seen
Milestone cycle time: days spent in each launch stage, and the variance across practices
Patient acquisition cost and payback by channel
Share of launch steps that are automated or self-serve rather than human-mediated
NP-reported experience of the launch process

sections.title: About the Role

That means everything customers see: GPU and cluster health, utilization, job-level telemetry, and InfiniBand fabric metrics. It also means the platform telemetry layer underneath, which powers Lambda's internal fleet operations and reliability work. You will partner daily with SRE (Site Reliability Engineering), fleet engineering, and the console and API (Application Programming Interface) teams to bring one coherent observability experience to customers and operators alike. This role reports to the Head of Platform Product Management.

Great product managers at Lambda are defined by three things: insight, influence, and execution. Insight means you look at the data, determine what it means for customers and business, and then figure out what to do about it. But, a great idea doesn’t mean anything in a vacuum. That is where influence comes in. Influence means you take that idea and get others to want to buy into it; you win over engineers, designers, executives, and partners without relying on authority. But a great idea that everyone is excited about doesn’t matter unless it is delivered to customers. Execution means you work with the right people to get the idea launched, then measure and iterate. We hire product managers who learn new domains fast and reason rigorously from evidence. Deep observability domain experience is a strong plus, but insight, influence, and execution are the bar.

bullets: Own the Observability Roadmap: Define and drive the product strategy for observability across Lambda's cloud, from single On-Demand GPU Instances to 1-Click Clusters at 64 to 1,024+ GPU scale.

Turn Telemetry into Product : Decide which signals customers see, including GPU and cluster health, utilization, job-level telemetry, and InfiniBand fabric metrics, and how they see them in the console and the Lambda Cloud API.

Ship Diagnostics That Answer the First Question : Build experiences that let a customer quickly distinguish their own code or configuration issues from platform problems such as a failing node or a degraded InfiniBand link.

Work Backwards : One of the key things customers want to know is if their application is causing issues or if it is Lambda. If it is Lambda, they want to know if it is within the expected tolerance. You will work with each product to define and productize SLIs, SLOs, and SLAs.

Build the Platform Telemetry Layer : Partner with SRE and fleet engineering to define the internal telemetry that powers fleet operations and reliability, so one data foundation serves both customers and operators.

Live with Customers : Spend time with AI research labs, AI startups, and enterprise ML (machine learning) teams to understand how they debug distributed training and inference, and turn that signal into decisions about what to build next.
Win the Room : Bring engineers, designers, and executives along on your roadmap through clear writing and evidence, not authority.
Measure and Iterate : Define the success metrics for observability features, instrument adoption, and use the results to decide what ships next.

As Omnea's AI Sales Engineer, you're the technical authority in our enterprise sales process, working alongside Sales to win some of the world's largest companies. You run discovery, build and direct demos and PoCs, and become the trusted technical advisor a prospect leans on to decide whether Omnea is real. ashby:robco:772e8125-0774-4186-9eb6-6a99.summary:
RobCo is building the category of Autonomous Industrial Robotics and we're doing it fast. We believe that automating the ordinary frees humans to do the extraordinary, and we're building the end-to-end robotics infrastructure to make that possible - hardware, software, and AI in one stack that just works.

As our (Senior) Robotic Sales Engineer, you are RobCo’s technical face to the customer and the technical lead on every deal you own, from the first customer call to a handover-ready solution. If something is broken, you fix it. If something can be automated, you build it.

sections.title: Your mission
paras: You work as a team with our Account Executives, and every technical question on the deal runs through you. You carry a quota together with your AE, and you win deals as a team.

Your job is to understand the customer’s process better than anyone else in the room, decide early what is feasible and what is not, and turn a real production problem into a clear, qualified automation case. You recommend the right automation approach and hand it over to our Solutions Development team without late surprises.

You work where modular robotics, software and AI come together, and you help bring physical AI from the lab into real production. You show customers what robots that perceive, learn and adapt can do in their plant today. You have direct access to the engineers, product managers and data behind our robots, and you help shape what we build next.

sections.title: What you will do
bullets: Qualify – Join discovery calls and site visits with your AE. Assess use cases early for technical fit, business value and risk, and say no when a deal does not fit.

Run requirement workshops – Lead structured on-site workshops with production, engineering and operations teams. Capture parts, processes, cycle times, layout, interfaces, safety and acceptance criteria.

Check feasibility – Make the first technical call on reach, payload, cycle time, gripping and vision. Use quick layouts, simulations and tests to back it up, and pull in Product or Solutions Development where needed.

Drive the concept – Turn workshop results into clear requirements and recommend the right automation approach. You own the collaboration with Solutions Development and Product until a complete, buildable concept is in place.
Be the technical face to the customer – Explain our robots and solutions to plant managers, engineers and executives in plain language. Run demos and support business cases and RaaS pricing inputs.
Close the loop – Feed field insights back to Product, so what customers need shapes what we build.

sections.title: What you bring
bullets: 3+ years where automation meets the customer: technical pre-sales, application engineering or automation projects
You want to be measured by results: you share a quota with your AE and push deals over the line
You have had your hands on robot cells, from grippers and vision to feeders, conveyors and safety, and you know what makes them run on the shop floor
You walk through a plant, watch a process for ten minutes and see where automation pays off
You lead conversations with confidence, whether with an operator on the line or the plant manager signing off the investment
You think in structure: after your workshop, the team can build on what you captured
You can sketch a layout or check reach in CAD or simulation (e.g. Autodesk Fusion, Visual Components)
You enjoy being on the road, around 30% of the time

sections.title: About RobCo
paras: Founded in Munich in 2020, RobCo leads the transition toward fully Autonomous Industrial Robotics. Our mission is to deploy RobCo in every factory - solving the industrial labor shortage through end-to-end robotics that just works. Powered by Physical AI, our solutions combine a scalable modular hardware architecture with intelligent software that continuously learns and improves, requiring zero upfront investment through our Robotics-as-a-Service (RaaS) model.

We solve our customers' most pressing pain points - labor shortage, cost pressure, workplace safety, and national reshoring - across the full spectrum of Autonomous Industrial Robotics. In October 2026, RobCo reached unicorn status with a valuation exceeding one billion US dollars, with its valuation doubling in less than nine months. With $200M raised from investors including Sequoia, Lightspeed, Lingotto, Kindred, Cherry Ventures, and the European Tech Collective, 225+ people globally, and 3.5M+ operating hours in the field, we are deploying robots in factories across Europe and the United States - with our US operations headquartered in Austin, TX, and our Bay Area Lab in San Francisco.

Don’t meet every single requirement? If you’re excited about this role but your past experience doesn’t align perfectly with every qualification in the job description, we encourage you to apply anyway. You may be just the right candidate for this or other roles.

ashby:sunday:38574000-365c-491a-a2b0-67e.summary:
At Sunday, we're developing personal robots to reclaim the hours lost to repetitive tasks. We're focused on an ambitious goal to make generalized robots broadly accessible, enabling households to take back quality time.

We have spent the last 2 years building a talented team, securing capital, and validating our technology. We are now seeking passionate individuals to join us in the next phase of our growth. If you are ready to apply your skills to the forefront of robotics innovation, we’d love to hear from you.

sections.title: What to Expect
paras: Sunday is putting robots into homes — around kids, pets, furniture, and families who haven't lived with a robot before. No regulatory body has defined what "safe" means for a home robot yet. We're defining it ourselves, and our brand depends on getting it right. You'll be our first product manager dedicated to trust and safety. You'll own the safety and privacy requirements for Memo end to end: what we test, what we promise users, and what we refuse to ship. You'll work across robot software, hardware, controls, ML, app, design, and operations to make safety a property of the whole system, not one team's checklist.

sections.title: What You'll Do
bullets: Own the safety and trust roadmap for Memo. Define what "safe enough to ship" means for each release, and hold the line on it.
Build the system-level safety case. Map failure modes across navigation, hardware, controls, task design, firmware, and user communications, and make sure each has an owner, a test, and a mitigation.
Work with engineering to define and track safety test coverage for every subsystem. Ensure firmware and software releases are validated against safety requirements before OTA.
Own data privacy for the product: what Memo records in the home, who can see it (including teleoperators), how long it's kept, and how users understand and control it.
Design how Memo behaves and communicates around kids, pets, and unexpected situations — stop conditions, warnings, recovery, and what the app tells users.

Set standards where none exist. Draw on adjacent industries (consumer durables, home fitness equipment, new category products, appliances) to build a safety framework fit for a home robot — without importing process that doesn't apply.
Run incident review. When something goes wrong in a home or the office, lead the investigation, root cause, and the change that follows.
Partner with product operations to turn real-home observations into safety requirements.

sections.title: What You'll Bring
bullets: 3+ years in product, safety, or quality roles on physical consumer products people touch and live with — think new category products, home fitness equipment, power tools, kitchen appliances, or similar. You've shipped hardware into homes where the standards were thin and you had to set them.

Not required: automotive, aerospace, or medical device background. While this is nice to have, we're looking for judgment in lightly regulated spaces, not fluency in pre-existing regulatory frameworks.
Detail-oriented. You read the test report, not the summary. You notice the edge case nobody listed.
Fast technical learner. You can pick up how a navigation stack, a controller, or a firmware release process works well enough to ask the right questions and spot gaps.
Strong judgment and a deep sense of responsibility. You'll make calls that affect families, and you treat that seriously. You're comfortable being the person who says "not yet."
Experience working with engineers on test plans, failure analysis, or release gating.
Familiarity with data privacy principles for connected consumer devices (cameras, in-home sensors).
Comfort with ambiguity at an early-stage company. You can write the first version of a safety standard that doesn't exist yet.

sections.title: What success looks like in 6 months
paras: Even if you don’t meet every single requirement, we encourage you to apply. Studies show that women and underrepresented groups often hold back unless they meet 100% of the criteria — we don’t want that to be the reason we miss out on great talent.
bullets: Memo has a written, system-level safety framework with owners and test coverage for every subsystem, used as a release gate.
Every firmware/software release passes a defined safety validation before OTA.
Data privacy policy for in-home recording and teleop is defined, implemented in the app, and understandable to users.
An incident review process is running, and beta learnings are feeding back into requirements.
Product, hardware, and engineering leads treat the T&S PM as the owner of "is this safe to ship."

sections.title: What to Expect
paras: Sunday is building home robots, and behind every robot is a set of tools that helps our teams operate, test and improve them. These tools support robot scheduling and maintenance, data labeling and quality review, robot testing, and customer support. As the number of robots we operate and the volume of data and testing grow, these tools are becoming critical to the business. You'll be our first product manager dedicated to internal tools, focusing on high-impact workflows that require coordination across multiple teams and users—not every internal tool. You'll own what we build and why for robot operators, data collection teams, technicians, machine learning engineers, product managers, customer support, quality assurance testers, and technical program managers.

sections.title: What You'll Do
bullets: Own the internal tools roadmap. Turn scattered, reactive requests into a coherent strategy that keeps maintenance costs down. Decide where tools should be combined and where different workflows or security requirements mean they should remain separate.

Prioritize tools for robot testing, robot operation and fleet management based on business impact and cross-team coordination needs. Fleet management includes robot scheduling, tracking repairs, delivering over-the-air software updates, and showing real-time robot location and health.

Define requirements for dedicated robot testing spaces: coordinate robots, people and space bookings, and support safety scanners, camera recording and live streaming. Build a path toward tests that can run without a person present.

Shape robot operation tools for distinct users: teams collecting data and evaluating robot performance, and testing, engineering and product teams running specific software versions or robot behaviors.
Work with data operations and machine learning teams to scale data labeling and quality review tools as data volume grows from in-house collection, external vendors and robot performance tests.
Learn directly from internal users. Shadow technicians, robot operators and data reviewers, and turn their workflows into clear requirements engineers can build from.

Set priorities with software engineering, data operations and other leads, and say no clearly. Help decide where AI agents that take actions on a user's behalf add value and where people should perform or control the work.
Define and track success metrics for each tool, such as adoption, time to resolve operational issues, and the amount of data reviewers can assess accurately.

Experience with hardware, robotics, fleets of connected devices, or machine learning data workflows such as labeling, quality review and model evaluation.
Strong discovery skills with non-technical users. You enjoy sitting next to a technician to learn how they work.

Strong technical grounding to work through tradeoffs with engineers on robot health and performance data, cloud services, data storage and access controls, and to make informed decisions about combining or separating tools.
Experience designing both AI-assisted workflows and workflows performed by people, with judgment about when to use AI agents and when to keep people in control.
Comfort with ambiguity at an early-stage company. You can write the first version of a problem statement that doesn't exist yet.
Bonus: experience with robot fleet management, remote robot operation, or test labs that connect real hardware to software-driven tests.

bullets: Robot fleet operations have a coherent roadmap and clear ownership, with tools combined where appropriate and adopted by operations and support teams.
Robot testing and operation tools have scoped plans and agreed staffing that address their distinct users and coordination needs, including a path toward tests that can run without a person present.

You won’t inherit an account-planning system or an expansion motion; rather, you’ll have the opportunity to build them. Working in a dedicated pod with a Customer Success Manager and a Customer Engineer, you own the executive relationship, the account plan, and the value, and you build the system that every Strategic Account Manager after you will inherit.

You own the number. In a high-net-dollar-retention business, that means running a disciplined scaling and expansion motion rather than hoping happy customers will grow: a documented thesis, a named budget owner, and realistic timing for every enterprise account in your portfolio. You lead the pod commercially and hold the executive relationship. You report to the COO, and the CEO reviews and countersigns commercials while you ramp. This is a senior, high-accountability role: we’re hiring someone who has owned enterprise scaling, expansion and renewal portfolios specifically, not something adjacent.

sections.title: What you own, and what you don’t
paras: You do not own day-to-day technical delivery or implementation (the Customer Engineer), or adoption mechanics and success-plan execution (the Customer Success Manager). You apply the pricing framework; you do not invent it: packaging and non-standard terms are the CEO’s, and non-standard requests escalate immediately. The pod model exists so each role can go deep rather than broad. Role clarity is a feature, not a limitation: if you find yourself doing someone else’s job, your job is to name it, not absorb it.
bullets: The number: renewal and expansion forecast for every account, and the account plan that gets you there. The pod’s commercial accountability sits here and only here.
Executive relationships: the exec sponsor relationship, the stakeholder map, and the renewal runway surfaced and worked long before the commercial conversation.

Airbnb was born in 2007 when two hosts welcomed three guests to their San Francisco home, and has since grown to over 5 million hosts who have welcomed over 2 billion guest arrivals in almost every country across the globe. Every day, hosts offer unique stays and experiences that make it possible for guests to connect with communities in a more authentic way.

Our Product Marketing Managers start with the guest and work backwards, turning product thinking, data, and research into strategy. They own outcomes end to end, lead cross-functional teams across engineering, design, data science, and program management, and stay close enough to the details to know when something is off.

sections.title: The Difference You Will Make
paras: As Product Marketing Manager for Social Features, you'll lead a new pod that turns guests' connections into reasons to come back to Airbnb. You'll own the features people use with their friends: the travel map and sharing it, group travel tools, recommendations from people you know, and how connections are woven across Airbnb to make the whole travel experience better. You'll own the outcome, not just the roadmap: you'll make the calls on scope and priority with a dedicated engineering lead, engineers, and design partner, and be accountable for the results. You'll take features from brief to launch, use experiment results to decide what to build next, and grow how often guests plan, book, and share trips with the people they know. You'll also write the product narrative that explains each release to leadership and to guests.

sections.title: A Typical Day
bullets: Work backwards from the guest: write crisp briefs and requirements for new features, each grounded in a real guest need and a clear definition of success
Prototype with AI first: build working prototypes yourself to explore ideas, test them with guests, and align the team in days rather than weeks
Drive execution with engineering, design, data science, and program management, from concept through launch and iteration, often with several features in flight at once

sections.title: Protecting Yourself from Recruitment Scams
paras: Anduril is committed to maintaining the integrity of our Talent acquisition process and the security of our candidates. We've observed a rise in sophisticated phishing and fraudulent schemes where individuals impersonate Anduril representatives, luring job seekers with false interviews or job offers. These scammers often attempt to extract payment or sensitive personal information.

bullets: No Financial Requests: Anduril will never solicit payment or demand personal financial details (such as banking information, credit card numbers, or social security numbers) at any stage of our hiring process. Our legitimate recruitment is entirely free for candidates.

Please always verify communications:


• Direct from Anduril: If you receive an email from one of our recruiters, it will only come from an @anduril.com address.

Via Agency Partner: If contacted by a recruiting agency for an Anduril role, their email will clearly identify their agency. If you suspect any suspicious activity, please verify the agency's authenticity by reaching out to contact@anduril.com .

Exercise Caution with Unsolicited Outreach: If you receive any communication that appears suspicious, contains grammatical errors, or makes unusual requests, do not engage. Always confirm the sender's email domain is @anduril.com before providing any personal information or clicking on links.

What to Do If You Suspect Fraud: Should you encounter any questionable or fraudulent outreach claiming to be from Anduril, please report it immediately to contact@anduril.com . Your proactive caution is invaluable in protecting your personal information and upholding the security and trustworthiness of our recruitment efforts.

Each one shapes how quickly a borrower gets an offer, how confidently we underwrite, and how smoothly a loan officer or partner gets a loan to funding. You’ll own the full lifecycle of these integrations, from improving the vendors we have and onboarding new ones to holding vendors accountable to the quality and SLAs our borrowers and partners depend on. You’ll build the monitoring that makes integration health visible across the company and use funnel, conversion, and quality data to decide where the next investment goes. This is a hands-on role: you write the requirements, run the vendor calls, and stay close to the details. You’ll also own the core product roadmap for new HELOC growth channels like SMB brokers, select fintech partnerships, and home improvement and solar contractors, early, high-upside channels where the product and partner workflow are still being defined.

You view payroll and tax implementation as a strategic asset that accelerates growth channels and enables GTM success. You bridge the gap between complex tax compliance and commercial scalability, ensuring operational excellence becomes a competitive advantage.

You are comfortable navigating high-stakes environments where precision is paramount, yet you possess the agility to adapt processes for rapid business expansion. You act as a translator, decoding intricate regulatory requirements into streamlined, customer-friendly workflows. By fostering deep cross-functional relationships, you ensure that the implementation journey not only secures the enterprise but also empowers our commercial teams to sell with confidence and speed.

sections.title: Go-to-Market & Commercial Enablement
bullets: Serve as strategic commercial partner to GTM teams (Sales & Customer Success), positioning implementation and operational excellence as a competitive advantage that accelerates deal closure and time-to-revenue.
Architect scalable, customer -centric implementation frameworks that operationalize complex tax and compliance requirements while removing friction for Sales and enhancing customer experience.
Lead complex customer migrations and platform transitions, managing risk with operational rigor while advocating for commercially viable, customer-centric solutions.
Define and execute the operational playbook for new growth channels, ensuring compliance and regulatory standards enable rather than impede commercial velocity.

sections.title: Operational Transformation & Scalability
bullets: Design and build scalable, repeatable operational processes and frameworks that enable growth without proportional increases in headcount or complexity.
Identify automation and efficiency opportunities across implementation, data management, and compliance workflows; drive technology-enabled solutions that reduce manual work and improve accuracy.
Lead operational transformation initiatives—centralizing fragmented processes, implementing new systems, or restructuring workflows to serve new business models and scale.
Establish operational metrics and KPIs that track efficiency, cost, quality, and customer impact; use data to drive continuous improvement.
Partner with Finance, Product, and Operations teams to align operational strategy with business growth plans and ensure scalability.

greenhouse:kaseya:6117152004.summary:

Our comprehensive platform helps organizations efficiently manage, secure, and automate their IT environments, driving operational efficiency and long-term business success.

Backed by Insight Partners , a leading global software investor, Kaseya has experienced sustained double-digit growth and continues to expand its global footprint. Today, Kaseya supports customers in more than 20 countries and manages over 15 million endpoints worldwide.

Founded in 2000, Kaseya was built by builders - and we're still building. We look for people who create rather than wait, who see a hard problem and lean in, and who treat challenges as raw material. At Kaseya, everyone plays a role in shaping the future of IT: whether you're in…

sections.title: About Kaseya
paras: We're building teams that grow, perform, and make an impact. If you're driven by the itch to make things better - a product, a process, a career - you'll fit right in.
At Kaseya, we don't just raise the bar. We build it.

sections.title: Position Summary
paras: Kaseya is seeking a n Account Manager, Enterprise Accounts to drive expansion within a portfolio of high value and complex customers. This role focuses on long term relationship development, strategic growth planning and navigating multi stakeholder enterprise environments. You will be responsible for identifying and executing large scale upsell and cross sell opportunities while acting as a trusted advisor to your clients.

sections.title: Key Responsibilities
bullets: Enterprise Account Growth and Strategy Own and develop a portfolio of enterprise level accounts, creating and executing multi year account plans that align Kaseya solutions with customer business objectives. Identify whitespace opportunities and build strategic roadmaps to drive sustained revenue growth.

Complex Deal Management Lead sophisticated sales cycles involving multiple stakeholders, procurement processes and executive level decision making. Manage deal strategy, negotiation and closing for high value, long cycle opportunities.

Executive Relationship Management Build and maintain strong relationships with senior stakeholders including C level executives. Position yourself as a trusted advisor by understanding business priorities, industry trends and organizational challenges.

Value Based Selling Translate Kaseya product suite into measurable business outcomes for enterprise clients. Develop tailored value propositions, business cases and ROI models to support expansion initiatives.

Customer Success and Adoption Leadership Partner closely with Customer Success to ensure successful onboarding, adoption and ongoing value realization. Monitor usage trends and proactively address risks to retention and growth.

Forecasting and Pipeline Management Maintain accurate forecasts while managing a robust pipeline of expansion opportunities. Use data driven insights to guide decision making and ensure predictability in long cycle enterprise deals.
Cross Functional Collaboration Collaborate with Sales Engineering, Product, Marketing and Customer Success teams to deliver seamless customer experiences and support complex solution deployments.

CRM and Account Intelligence Leverage Salesforce and account intelligence tools to track engagement, pipeline and account health. Maintain detailed records to support strategic planning and reporting.

sections.title: Required Qualifications
bullets: 4+ years of B2B sales or account management experience, with at least 1 years focus on enterprise or large mid market accounts
Proven success managing long sales cycles and closing high value, complex deals
Experience engaging and selling to senior decision makers including C level stakeholders

greenhouse:launchdarkly:8042026003.summary: LaunchDarkly is the runtime control plane for the AI software development lifecycle (AI-SDLC). Thousands of engineering organizations, including more than a quarter of the Fortune 500, use LaunchDarkly to ship, measure, and control every change that reaches production, whether it is written by people or by AI. Feature management built the company. The next chapter is bigger: as the cost of writing code falls and the volume of change outpaces human review, the constraint is moving from writing software to controlling it. LaunchDarkly is building the critical infrastructure for the AI-SDLC. Customers build their own software factories. We build the rails they run on.

sections.title: About the Job:
paras: We are hiring the leader of Product Management for LaunchDarkly. Reporting to the Chief Product Officer, you will own the product management organization end to end: the people, operating system, roadmap commitments, and commercial outcomes across every product pillar. You will sit at the technology leadership table as the Product Management peer to the heads of Engineering and Product Design.

The CPO sets the company’s product vision and strategic direction. You will build and run the product organization that turns that direction into a coherent portfolio, shipped outcomes, customer adoption, and revenue growth. This is a hands-on operating role for a product leader who knows how to build the machine, make the tradeoffs, and finish the work.

sections.title: Responsibilities:
bullets: Lead cross-functional product leadership. Serve as the product counterpart to Engineering, Product Design, Marketing, Sales, Customer Success, and Finance. Resolve cross-functional tradeoffs, establish shared commitments, and ensure LaunchDarkly presents one coherent product strategy to customers and the market.

Build and lead the product management organization. Design the organization intentionally, allocate resources effectively, maintain a high talent bar, build succession plans, and establish clear ownership for every product surface a customer or sales representative may ask about.

Drive roadmap delivery across every product pillar. Lead execution across Enterprise, Foundation, Observability, Experimentation, Agent Control, Automation, and the platform beneath them. Build a culture of doing what we say we are going to do.

Create portfolio discipline without slowing the company down. Ensure new bets enter the portfolio through explicit decisions rather than hallway conversations, while preserving the flexibility to respond to market changes. Marketing dates should be commitments the product organization can confidently support.

Drive finishing. A product is not done when version one ships; it is done when the team has iterated based on learning. A launch is not done when it ships; it is done when the field is amplifying it. A process is not done when it is written; it is done when it creates leverage for the team.

Own packaging execution and commercial outcomes. Lead how pricing and packaging land in the product and in the field so every representative can sell the full platform and every pillar contributes to its commercial goals.

Stay close to customers and the field. Spend time with the largest customers and most demanding evaluators, translate what you learn into product decisions, and build a process that brings customer and field insight into the roadmap at scale.

Use AI to increase product and engineering leverage. Help the organization adopt AI-assisted development and product practices in ways that increase delivery speed while maintaining quality and judgment.

sections.title: What Success Looks Like in Your First Year:
bullets: The organization is complete. The leadership model is in place, product lines have the right pillar leadership, spans and layers are intentional, decision rights are clear, succession risks are understood, and the organization can continue to scale.
Delivery increases every quarter. Shipped output per team rises quarter over quarter as AI-assisted development compounds, with quality holding.
The operating system runs without the CPO driving it. Reviews, check-ins, launch briefs, and NPI happen on cadence and at a consistent bar.
The portfolio is staffed. Every initiative in flight has an explicit staffing decision and plan behind it.
The numbers move. Activation, attach, activity, and expansion targets for each pillar respond to the organization’s inputs.
The team is stronger than you found it. Product managers have more leverage, complementary strengths are valued over a uniform mold, and every hire raises the bar.

sections.title: About You:
bullets: You are direct, decisive, and high-agency. You identify a problem, propose a fix, and act unless someone tells you not to.

You are a relentless simplifier, not a caretaker. When you find friction, your instinct is to remove process rather than add it. You know how to run a company of this size like a small company that ships.

You are a builder of people and move quickly on people problems. Product leaders who have worked for you say you made them better and would work for you again. You raise the bar clearly, promote based on evidence, and do not allow known performance problems to persist.

You are comfortable challenging a strategy and turning it into a sequenced portfolio. You can tell the story of an idea you pushed back on, how you used evidence to make the call, and how you maintained the relationship.
You write clearly and make decisions. You use written argument to create alignment, expect strong writing from your team, and end meetings with a decision.

You are customer-oriented and commercially grounded. You can move from a conversation with a developer or data scientist to a discussion with an executive buyer or sales leader without losing the thread.

greenhouse:lightningai:8208545003.summary:
Lightning AI is the company behind PyTorch Lightning. Founded in 2019, we build an end-to-end platform for developing, training, and deploying AI systems—designed to take ideas from research to production with less friction.

Through our merger with Voltage Park, a neocloud and AI Factory, Lightning AI combines developer-first software with cost-efficient, large-scale compute. Teams get the tools they need for experimentation, training, and production inference, with security, observability, and control built in.

We serve solo researchers, startups, and large enterprises. Lightning AI operates globally with offices in New York City, San Francisco, Seattle, and London, and is backed by Coatue, Index Ventures, Bain Capital Ventures, and Firstminute.

sections.title: The Way We Work
paras: The people who thrive here are builders who move fast, communicate openly, take ownership, and continuously improve themselves, their teams, and our company. Here's what that looks like in practice:
bullets: Move with Urgency: We move quickly, make thoughtful decisions, and keep momentum. We value action over perfection and learn by shipping.
Take Ownership: We own outcomes, not just our individual work. We make decisions that move the company forward and follow through.
Communicate Openly: We communicate directly, seek to understand, and create clarity for others. Honest conversations help us move faster together.
Build Great Teams: We lead by example, empower others, and create healthy teams where people can do their best work.
Raise the Bar: We're always improving ourselves. We learn from feedback, consistently challenge ourselves to grow, and focus on the work that matters most.
Think Long-Term: We design for what's next. We create scalable systems, simplify complexity, and use AI and automation to amplify our impact.

sections.title: What We're Looking For
paras: Lightning AI is seeking a Solutions Engineering Manager to lead a team of presales Solutions Engineers who win and expand our AI/ML platform deals, with customers ranging from AI-native startups to research labs and Fortune 500 enterprises. This is a true player-coach role: you'll build and develop the team and own technical win rate across your segment, while personally running a set of strategic deals as lead SE from discovery to technical close.

This role requires hands-on AI/ML experience. Our buyers are ML engineers, researchers, and platform teams, and they can tell quickly whether someone has trained and deployed models themselves. You'll need to earn that trust in your own deals and set the technical bar for your team.

Your SEs are the technical voice in the sales cycle. They run discovery with ML leads and platform teams, design solutions for training, fine-tuning, and inference workloads, and earn the technical decision through demos and proofs of concept. You'll partner with Sales leadership as an equal and be the bridge from the field to Product and Engineering.

sections.title: What You'll Do
bullets: Hire, onboard, and develop Solutions Engineers who combine hands-on AI/ML depth with strong customer presence, and run 1:1s, career plans, and performance reviews that build a culture of ownership, curiosity, and craft
Coach the team on discovery, solution design, demos, objection handling, and POC execution, joining calls, giving specific feedback, and raising the team's ML technical depth

Own technical win rate, POC conversion, and SE contribution to pipeline and bookings, aligning SE coverage with AE territories and partnering with Sales leadership on forecasting, deal strategy, and account planning
Run your own book of strategic deals as lead SE, from discovery and solution design through demos, POCs, executive technical briefings, and security and procurement reviews
Set the standard for POCs, with clear success criteria, scoped timelines, and a crisp technical close

Build repeatable playbooks and reusable assets, including discovery frameworks, reference architectures, demo environments, and POC templates that show Lightning on real workloads such as LLM fine-tuning, distributed training, and model serving
Bring structured field feedback and competitive insight to Product and Engineering, and partner with Customer Success on clean handoffs so technical wins become long-term adoption and expansion

sections.title: What You Need
bullets: 5+ years in presales Solutions Engineering, Sales Engineering, or a similar customer-facing technical role, including 2+ years managing SEs

Hands-on AI/ML experience: you have trained, fine-tuned, or deployed models yourself, whether as an ML engineer, data scientist, researcher, or a deeply technical ML-focused SE, and can explain the tradeoffs across the lifecycle from training to inference

Working fluency in the modern AI/ML stack, including PyTorch, GPU compute, distributed training, and LLM fine-tuning and serving, deep enough to build and debug demos and POCs yourself, not just guide them

A record of hitting team targets and winning complex, technical enterprise deals for AI/ML or ML infrastructure products such as ML platforms, MLOps tools, or AI compute, using MEDDIC or a similar qualification methodology
Experience engaging ML buyer personas such as ML engineers, data scientists, researchers, and ML platform engineers
Working knowledge of cloud infrastructure (AWS, GCP, or Azure), Kubernetes and containers, and enterprise needs such as SSO, VPC deployment, and data security
Strong executive presence and written communication, with the range to pitch to a CTO and go deep on model architecture with an ML team on the same day
A coaching mindset and the judgment to know when to lead from the front and when to let your team run

greenhouse:lirio:8208575003.summary: Lirio is a technology/software company that provides expertise in a variety of behavioral science domains (e.g., behavioral economics, social psychology, public health), data science, and machine learning to drive consumer engagement, close gaps in preventive and chronic care, and promote health and well-being across an individual’s lifespan. Lirio’s behavior change AI platform unites behavioral science with advanced artificial intelligence (AI) to deliver Precision Nudging health interventions. Precision Nudging is the application of behavioral science to health interventions personalized by AI to each individual that overcome barriers to action at the right time and place for scalable, behavior change.

sections.title: Position Summary
paras: The Lead Product Manager, Agentic AI owns the evolution of Lirio's decisioning, orchestration, and agentic AI capabilities — the core of how Lirio serves as the behavioral intelligence layer powering enterprise healthcare consumer engagement. This role leads product strategy for Lirio's Agent Framework, Person Model, Conversational AI, and Self-Service/Studio capabilities, translating behavioral science and AI-driven intelligence into coordinated, personalized interventions delivered through the channels clients already use. They anticipate market trends, consumer needs, and emerging AI capabilities and translate them into scalable product capabilities and clear product requirements. Partnering with Engineering, AI/ML, Behavioral Science, Security, Growth , and other Product colleagues , they align teams around the product strategy and roadmap for Lirio's A gentic AI capabilities, making well-informed product and responsible-AI trade-offs .

sections.title: Essential Duties & Responsibilities
paras: Cross-Functional Leadership & Communication
bullets: Envision, articulate, and deliver the agentic AI product strategy and product focus areas that shape Lirio's position as an AI Behavior Change leader in the healthcare market.

Develop a deep understanding of customer and business challenges, market dynamics, and emerging AI/agentic capabilities by engaging customers and stakeholders, monitoring the competitive and regulatory landscape, and participating in industry forums, and use those insights to shape product strategy.
Critically evaluate information from multiple sources and apply systems thinking to prioritize across competing demands, making rigorous, evidence-based trade-offs.

Own Lirio's decisioning and orchestration capabilities as products, defining how behavioral and AI-driven intelligence becomes coordinated, personalized interventions across the channels clients already use.
Own the product roadmap for Lirio's Agent Framework and Large Behavioral Model.
Own the product strategy for Lirio's Conversational AI capabilities.
Own the Self-Service/Studio product roadmap, including the Content sub-identity, growing configurability and reducing reliance on manual delivery.

Define clear product requirements for personalization logic, intervention sequencing, and experimentation, and make sound product trade-offs in partnership with engineering, data science, and behavioral science.

sections.title: Qualifications
bullets: 8+ years of progressive product management experience, including ownership of AI-driven, personalization, or decisioning products, with demonstrated success setting strategy, influencing senior stakeholders, navigating product and AI trade-offs, and delivering scalable capabilities across clients or markets.
Bachelor’s degree in technical or related field required. Master’s degree preferred.
Proven track record of leading complex AI/ML or agentic product initiatives from discovery through delivery with measurable impact on adoption, engagement, and business outcomes.
Strong product fundamentals: discovery, requirements definition, outcomes-driven prioritization, success metrics, and using data to validate assumptions and demonstrate impact.

Strong systems thinking and decision-making rigor, with the ability to reason across personalization logic, agent behavior, data, and downstream business/health outcomes, weighing trade-offs against evidence in ambiguous, high-stakes situations.
Proven ability to set technical and AI product direction that is adopted across multiple teams, influencing without direct authority.
Strong communicator who distills complex technical and AI concepts for both technical and non-technical audiences, including senior executives.
Understanding of the healthcare market and buyers (payers, providers, employers, retail health) highly preferred.

paras: We prioritize candidate safety. Please be aware that official communication will only come from @medallion.co email addresses.

sections.title: About the Role
paras: We’re looking for a Staff Product Manager to lead Payer Enrollment, responsible for getting providers enrolled with insurers so they can see patients and get paid. Enrollment is Medallion’s largest and fastest-growing opportunity and the most direct line between our software and a customer’s revenue: until a provider is enrolled, they can’t bill, and every day of delay is lost income for the organizations we serve.

This is a commercially minded product role, led through clear goals and metrics. Designers and engineers carry the bulk of feature development. You make sure we build the right things, and that what ships gets adopted, gets sold, and changes outcomes for customers. Success means Payer Enrollment grows faster, and our largest customers champion Medallion.

This role reports to the Chief Product Officer and base compensation for this role may land between $200,000-$250,000. In addition to base salary, Medallion offers equity, and benefits as part of the total compensation package. Many factors are considered when determining pay including: market data, geographic location, skills, qualifications, experience, and level.

sections.title: Responsibilities
bullets: Set product strategy and goals. Plan for a 12 to 18 month horizon, based on what customers and the market tell us. Choose the metrics that show whether it’s working. Use them to set priorities and report progress.
Guide sales strategy. Help decide where our sales team should focus. Join deals with our largest prospects. Give sales and customer success teams the market knowledge they need to sell.

Keep customers happy. Work directly with our largest customers. Learn what they need and share it with the team. Plan launches with marketing and operations, and track whether customers use what we build.
Build with AI. Use AI tools to build prototypes and ship code yourself. Work closely with engineers on technical decisions.

Comfortable writing SQL, building your own dashboards, and shipping code with AI tools

In the 1940s, Florence Knoll helped transform modern design by approaching interiors as complete systems rather than collections of individual objects. A beautiful chair wasn't enough. The architecture, furniture, materials, and the ways people moved through a space all needed to work together. Her approach, known as the Knoll Planning Unit, helped redefine how we think about modern spaces.

At Mercury, we're approaching lending with a similar philosophy. We're not just bringing financing products to market. We're thinking about how lending fits into a broader financial experience, helping ambitious companies access the capital they need to grow, without having to look beyond their financial home.

sections.title: In this role, you'll:
bullets: Shape Mercury's lending marketing strategy. Identify our biggest market opportunities, define target audiences, establish competitive positioning, and prioritize where we can have the greatest impact.
Turn customer and market insights into action. Lead customer research and competitive analysis to uncover unmet needs, inform product priorities, and influence business decisions.
Own positioning and messaging for our lending products. Translate complex financial concepts into clear, compelling stories that help businesses understand the value of Mercury's lending offerings.
Lead go-to-market strategy for lending products and initiatives. Partner with Product, Credit, Growth, and Revenue to bring new capabilities to market and drive adoption of existing offerings.

Build scalable go-to-market motions that drive growth. Work with Sales, Relationship Management, and Growth to reach the right customers, equip revenue teams, and help more qualified businesses access financing.
Measure what's working and find opportunities to improve. Use customer feedback, performance data, and business results to refine our approach and identify new growth opportunities.

Exceptional product marketing fundamentals, including customer research, competitive analysis, positioning, messaging, and product launches.
Strong commercial instincts. You understand how product marketing contributes to acquisition, adoption, and revenue, and can connect your decisions to measurable business impact.

Experience in lending, business financing, B2B fintech, financial services, or another complex product category is a strong plus, but isn't required. We're especially interested in people who have demonstrated exceptional product marketing judgment.

greenhouse:mixpanel:8354540.summary: Mixpanel is the leading product intelligence and analytics platform, trusted by more than 29,000 companies to help understand how people use the products they build. By combining powerful analytics with AI that knows your business, Mixpanel helps teams see what’s working, diagnose what’s not, and decide what to build next. Learn more at mixpanel.com .

sections.title: About the Role
paras: The core of Mixpanel’s value to customers has always been great data. We’re in an exciting moment for the way our users are thinking about and working with product data, and we need help figuring out how our position in the data infrastructure stack evolves. That’s why we’re hiring a fantastic Product Manager for Mixpanel Data.

In this role, you'll own Mixpanel's strategy and roadmap for where we sit in the data landscape - how our data architecture evolves, where we build versus integrate versus get out of the way, and what it means for Mixpanel to work with data that increasingly lives outside our walls as well as inside them. This is a pathfinding role: a large part of the job is turning ambiguous technical and business tradeoffs into a clear point of view, a roadmap, and decisions the engineering and leadership team can act on.

sections.title: What You'll Do
bullets: Define and drive Mixpanel's strategy and roadmap for how the product evolves alongside customers' data warehouses, lakes, and the broader modern data stack
Turn complex, ambiguous architecture and business tradeoffs into a clear recommendation, grounded in customer evidence, competitive context, and business impact
Partner closely with engineering leadership on build-vs-integrate-vs-partner decisions that shape Mixpanel's data architecture for years to come
Talk directly to customers and prospects to understand how their data infrastructure and workflows are changing, and translate that into product bets
Build the business case for infrastructure-level investments, making the ROI of foundational, long-horizon work legible to leadership
Define how Mixpanel's data model, governance, and metadata need to evolve to support deeper analysis and a growing product portfolio
Align engineering, design, and go-to-market teams around a shared strategic point of view, with clear, written communication
Define and track the metrics that tell you whether the strategy is working, and course-correct as new evidence comes in

sections.title: What We're Looking For
bullets: 5+ years of hands-on product management experience, including ownership of technically complex, infrastructure- or platform-level problems
Direct experience with the modern data stack — data warehouses, data lakes, ETL/ELT, or data platform tooling — as a builder, user, or product owner
Comfort operating in ambiguity, with a track record of synthesizing competing technical and business inputs into a clear strategic point of view
Experience partnering closely with engineering on architecture-level tradeoffs, not just feature scoping
Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to bring technical and non-technical audiences along on a strategic narrative
Experience using AI tools in product management workflows (e.g., competitive research, prototyping)

sections.title: Nice to Have
bullets: Experience at a data infrastructure, data platform, or analytics company
Hands-on experience with data warehouses/lakehouses (e.g., Snowflake, BigQuery, Databricks) or open data formats
Experience writing production-grade software
Experience designing products using tools like Figma, Sketch, or Abstract

Identity platforms: Okta, Microsoft Entra, Duo, Auth0, Ping, and custom IAM stacks.

greenhouse:peregrinetechnologies:4715237.summary: Backed by leading Silicon Valley investors, Peregrine helps public safety organizations, state and local and governments, federal agencies , and private-sector institutions address society’s challenges with unprecedented speed and accuracy. Our AI-enabled platform turns siloed and disconnected data into operational intelligence — instantly surfacing mission-critical information to empower better, faster decisions that improve outcomes at every touchpoint. Today Peregrine supports hundreds of customers across 30+ states and two countries, serving more than 125 million people — and we’re amplifying our impact as we expand into the enterprise and internationally.

sections.title: The role
paras: Peregrine's value lives below the surface. We unify dozens of disconnected data sources, resolve entities, preserve context, and ground AI in that unified picture. The visible product is a small fraction of the work that drives customer outcomes. The harder, more durable value lives in the integration layer underneath. This is a builder role for someone excited to make that layer legible, defensible, and competitive for audiences ranging from public safety operators to federal evaluators to commercial technical buyers. The work starts from technical depth; everything else in the role builds on it. Peregrine is creating a category without established head-to-head competitors, so a core part of this role is teaching the market what to evaluate.

You will be the founding Technical Product Marketer, reporting to the VP of Product Marketing. There is no technical marketing foundation yet; you will build it from scratch for prospects, analysts, and sellers, and Solutions Marketing will adapt it for specific verticals and audiences. This role owns product positioning, messaging, and competitive narrative across the platform: what Peregrine claims, how those claims are defended, and what the market learns to evaluate.

sections.title: In this role you will...
bullets: Own technical positioning and messaging for the core platform: data unification, entity resolution, AI grounding, integration architecture, and the operational AI layer built on that foundation.

Demystify the category itself. Build the first-principles content that explains why unifying operational data, resolving entities, and grounding AI are genuinely hard problems, why common approaches fall short, and what an architecture built for this work actually requires.

Build the technical content library the rest of marketing and sales depends on: technical whitepapers, architecture briefs, security and compliance content, and AI substantiation that holds up under public, legal, and political scrutiny.
Turn competitive technical intelligence into asymmetric sales tools and teardowns that hold up against horizontal data platforms, operational AI platforms, and AI point solutions.
Contribute product-led narratives to high-visibility launches, with focus on the technical proof points that make each launch credible.

sections.title: What you'll bring
bullets: 5+ years of work experience across engineering and product marketing. A technical foundation is required: a computer science or related degree, an early-career engineering role, or equivalent built depth. You can read a spec, work through a data model, and defend an architectural claim to our CTO.
Product marketing experience in B2B SaaS, AI, or data infrastructure. You have authored positioning where none existed and built competitive teardowns that moved real deals.

Management consulting experience can add supporting depth in structured problem decomposition, analytical rigor, and the ability to learn complex domains fast. However it does not substitute for the technical foundation.
Exceptional writing. You can produce technical content that holds up to a technical reader and translates cleanly for a non-technical one.
Comfort moving between deep technical conversations with engineers and business outcome conversations with executives, without losing either audience.

sections.title: What success looks like
bullets: Build a working mental model of Peregrine's platform, deep enough to defend technical claims independently across the stack.
Sellers reach for your content unprompted in deal cycles.
Peregrine has a defensible technical narrative against horizontal data platforms, operational AI platforms, and AI point solutions that sellers and prospects can articulate consistently.
Peregrine's AI claims hold up under technical and security reviews and public scrutiny.
Build trusted partnerships with Product, Engineering, Forward Deployed Engineering, Solutions Engineering and Solutions Marketing.
Influence the product-led narrative for major launches.

sections.title: What You'll Do:

greenhouse:topsteptrader:8039658003.summary:
The High Risk Trader Onboarding Analyst is an operational investigator within the Onboarding & Identity Operations team, responsible for reviewing elevated-risk Identity Verification (IDV) exceptions, performing Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD), and conducting thorough financial crime screenings across global trader accounts.

Serving as the primary operational intake for elevated risk profiles, this role investigates Tier-2 escalations from front-line onboarding teams that exceed standard verification logic, such as suspected synthetic identity indicators, document tampering, multi-jurisdictional tax discrepancies (W-8/W-9), and potential sanctions hits. Operating within established operating frameworks and investigative templates, you will clear routine screening alerts, assemble structured case packages for Enforcement review, and escalate novel fraud vectors or complex corporate…

sections.title: Key Responsibilities
bullets: IDV & CIP Escalation Review: Review and disposition Tier-2 identity verification escalations referred by front-line onboarding analysts. Investigate flagged accounts exhibiting synthetic identity traits, digital document manipulation, device/IP anomalies, or unverified registration data against established risk rubrics.

Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) Execution: Perform structured EDD investigations on elevated-risk traders. Collect, review, and evaluate baseline financial documentation to verify identity legitimacy and account eligibility.

Investigative Case Packaging: Compile clear, evidence-based case files summarizing identity telemetry, document discrepancies, and risk rationales. Submit structured findings to Senior Analysts, Compliance, and Enforcement teams for account restrictions, suspensions, or closure.

Triage & Senior Escalation: Identify high-complexity scenarios, such as organized multi-account fraud rings, highly layered entity structures, or emergent attack vectors, and route them with complete preliminary findings to the Senior High Risk Trader Onboarding Analyst.
Audit Trail & Record Governance: Maintain precise, audit-ready case notes and rationale logs in internal case management systems to satisfy QA benchmarks and internal compliance audits.

Workflow Feedback: Identify recurring friction points, false-positive trends, and operational bottlenecks within EDD workflows, providing actionable data to Senior Analysts to help refine templates and SOPs.

sections.title: Required Qualifications and Key Competencies
bullets: Experience: 1-3 years of direct operational experience in AML/KYC, Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD), financial crime investigations, or fraud operations within fintech, digital brokerage, or a regulated financial institution.
IDV & Risk Tool Fluency: Working knowledge of modern identity verification platforms (e.g., Persona, Jumio, Veriff, Onfido) and screening databases (e.g., LexisNexis, World-Check, ComplyAdvantage).
Investigative Rationale & Writing: Strong written communication skills, with a track record of authoring concise, objective, and defensible case narratives.
Adherence to Established Frameworks: High operational discipline and sound judgment to evaluate qualitative risk signals within structured SOPs, knowing precisely when and how to escalate edge cases.
Attention to Detail: Acute visual and analytical attention to detail to spot minor indicators of document alteration, metadata inconsistencies, and synthetic identity markers.
Asynchronous Collaboration: Ability to manage high-priority investigation queues independently and partner cross-functionally across remote compliance, legal, and operational teams.

Clear Communication & Collaboration: Strong written and verbal communication skills. Ability to accurately document case notes, clearly summarize issues for escalation, and collaborate effectively within a remote team environment.
